text:
Alex Li: Hey team — quick q about vision benefits: I just got progressive (varifocal) lenses last week. The plan docs say 'lenses covered' but I can't tell if progressives count as covered vs an upgrade. Can I get reimbursed? Do I need pre-approval? Filing steps? @people-ops
Karla (People Ops): Hey Alex — congrats. Short answer: it depends on the plan and whether you used an in-network provider. Which plan are you on (Basic vs Enhanced)?
Alex Li: I'm on Enhanced (picked during open enrollment). I bought lenses at a local independent optician (not Visionworks). Paid $270 for the lenses and $130 for anti-glare coating.
Morgan (Benefits): Thanks — with Enhanced, standard single/double vision lenses have a $25 copay. Progressives are usually considered a premium lens option; we provide a $120 allowance toward premium lenses. Anti-glare/coatings are typically eligible up to the allowance but sometimes considered add-ons. You can cover the remainder with FSA/HSA or OOP.
Karla (People Ops): Filing steps: 1) Get an itemized receipt showing lens type, frame (if applicable), and line-item prices. 2) Attach your eyeglass prescription. 3) Complete the vision claim form on the benefits portal (or include the required fields in an email). Submit via: https://benefits.redwood.com/claims or email claims@benefits.redwood.com with subject 'Vision claim - <Your Name>'.
Alex Li: Do I need prior authorization for progressives? Also how does out-of-network reimbursement work (I used an independent shop)?
Morgan (Benefits): No prior auth required for lenses. Out-of-network claims are reimbursed up to the plan's UCR (usual, customary, reasonable) rate — you pay any difference. Typical processing time is 7–14 business days after the claim is received. Keep originals for 90 days in case they ask.
Morgan (Benefits): Sample email payload (copy/paste):
```
To: claims@benefits.redwood.com
Subject: Vision claim - Alex Li (EmpID 04562)
Body: Full name: Alex Li
DOB: 1992-04-12
Employee ID: 04562
Date of service: 2026-03-03
Provider: ClearView Optics (Dr. Maya Patel)
Attachments: itemized_receipt.pdf, prescription.pdf
```
benefits-bot: Auto-reply: Claim received (V-20260315-4321). Estimated processing: 10 business days.
Alex Li: Great — last q: can I use FSA to cover the remaining $160 out-of-pocket?
Morgan (Benefits): Yes — FSA/HSA funds can be used for eligible vision expenses. Upload the EOB/paid receipt to the FSA portal after claim payment, or submit directly to the FSA admin if you want quicker reimbursement. If you'd like, I can walk you through the upload steps or set a 10-min screen share. :thumbsup:
Karla (People Ops): Filed a note on your benefits record, Alex. LMK if you want help assembling the docs.
